clue.text: Hide from the old writer's relatives

parts.note: Charles Lamb, the essayist of Essays of Elia, is the old writer; his possessive gives the letters
kin are one's family or relations

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover among the family members of a long-dead author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for an animal's skin. Charles Lamb (1775-1834) was an English essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep's pelt, with its wool, is a kind of leather or animal skin.

clue.text: Instruction to have fewer commitments

parts.note: fewer means less
having a lot on means having many commitments, so on stands for them

explanation.surface: Advice to take on fewer obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: A class or a piece of teaching is a unit of tuition.

clue.text: Striker has encountered about everything

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to have met someone is to have encountered them
all means everything

explanation.surface: A footballer has met with the whole lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but here it is a wooden hammer, as used in croquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden hammer is a tool for hitting things.

clue.text: Visa's forged by our rescuer

indicators.note: forged means faked or shaped anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter, leaving the word visa

explanation.surface: A rescuer has a counterfeit travel permit made by us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges VISA to SAVI; 'by' simply joins it to OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saves another from danger is their deliverer.

clue.text: Unimportant provision in the Riot Act

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A trivial clause inside the law against public disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read out to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter stands for a very small amount, so a tiny provision is trifling.

clue.text: Forbid to crib — it is meant to be difficult to grasp

definitions.text: meant to be difficult to grasp

parts.note: to bar something is to prohibit it
a crib is a child's cot, a small bed

explanation.surface: A ban on a baby's cot, explained as something designed to be hard to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbed wire carries spikes precisely so that nobody can take hold of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitted with hooks or spikes is designed so that hands cannot grip it.

clue.text: A mother social-worker finds hard

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
an ant is a social insect and a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A parent who is also a social worker finds things tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social-worker' is the worker ant, a social insect, not a welfare officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once named a legendary unbreakable stone, so it means unyielding.

clue.text: Some money stolen to get ammunition

parts.note: bucks are dollars, a sum of money
hot means stolen in slang

explanation.surface: Stolen cash is used to buy bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead pellets fired from a shotgun are a kind of shot or ammunition.

clue.text: No longer with us: a strange case indeed

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes into another

parts.note: deed is taken as written, from the second part of indeed

indicators.note: strange means odd or abnormal, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peculiar legal matter concerning someone who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'indeed' as 'in deed': 'strange' rearranges CASE to CEAS, placed 'in' DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has passed away is no longer living among us.

clue.text: It's a veal stew to make one drool

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook boasts that a veal casserole will make the diner's mouth water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' turns ITSAVEAL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing saliva in anticipation of food is to slobber or dribble.

clue.text: Some tropical cichlids needing water with a lime content

definitions.text: needing water with a lime content

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An aquarist notes that certain tropical fish need hard, chalky water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things containing or relating to calcium, the element in lime and chalk.

clue.text: After someone's job!

parts.note: post means after, as in postwar
a man is someone, a person; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone is after another person's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a letter carrier comes after you to do his job of delivering.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail carrier's round brings him to each person's door as part of his work.

clue.text: Woolly robe on sprightly monarch

indicators.note: woolly means muddled or confused, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lively king puts on a fleecy gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' rearranges ROBEON. Sprightly here means sprite-like: the answer is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fairy king rules the sprites of the wood, making him a monarch of sprightly folk.

clue.text: Girl finds injured seal in the Pacific

parts.note: Cora is a girl's name

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl comes across a wounded seal while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges SEAL to LSEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This body of water lies off north-east Australia, an arm of the great ocean.

clue.text: Collar, plus some fruit, in the luggage

parts.note: to collar or bag something is to seize it
a gage is a plum, as in greengage

explanation.surface: A neck piece plus some fruit stashed in a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' is a verb meaning catch, not a shirt neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags and cases taken on a journey are a traveller's belongings.

clue.text: Sitting on chest, member of rowing team can take you across the water

definitions.text: can take you across the water

indicators.note: one piece placed after the other in the across answer, as if seated upon it

parts.note: the breast is the chest
the stroke is the oarsman who sets the pace in a rowing eight

explanation.surface: A rower perched on someone's torso will ferry a passenger across.
explanation.walkthrough: The rowing talk tempts towards a boat, but the definition is a swimming style that gets you across.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming technique propels a person through water, so it can get them to the far side.

clue.text: Habitation hidden in wild glen

indicators.note: letters disguised within a jumble, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dwelling tucked away in a rough valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' tempts a hidden word, but WILDGLEN is rearranged whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where people live is a home or abode.

clue.text: Dashing event — or does it prove to lack excitement?

definitions.meaning: a horse race with no jumps, all running

definitions.text: does it prove to lack excitement?
definitions.meaning: a race that falls flat is a dull contest

explanation.definitionFit: A horse race without hurdles is a sprint, and a dull contest sounds like one without fizz.

clue.text: Light work, for them

parts.note: echoes the proverb that many helpers make a task easy: eager helpers are those for whom labour becomes light

explanation.definitionFit: Keen helpers ease any task, as the saying about many hands making light work goes.

clue.text: The diggings hold silver, I at first assume

indicators.note: this piece goes at the front
one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a mine is a place for digging
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A prospector supposes the mine holds silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The diggings' is a single place to dig, not a set of lodgings, which British slang also calls diggings.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something is to picture it as true in one's mind.

clue.text: Spotted clergyman accepting the forbidden fruit

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree
Eve's forbidden fruit is traditionally an apple

explanation.surface: A priest is seen taking the fruit from Eden's tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like seen, but it means mottled.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with patches of colour, as a horse can be, means mottled.

clue.text: Fish, the second caught by a politician, I understand

parts.note: S is short for second
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician says he caught a fish in second place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understand' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails are a seafood dish.

clue.text: Official summons? The ambassador will wriggle out of it

parts.note: a writ is a court order summoning someone
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: An ambassador handed a legal summons tries to escape it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of it' is a link to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist and squirm is to writhe in discomfort.

clue.text: Greatly distressed in hospital, with abnormal lack of energy

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
distressed means agitated or battered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital is very upset and feels drained of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges GREATLY, and 'in' places H for hospital within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names drowsy sluggishness, a torpor far beyond ordinary tiredness.

clue.text: Unoccupied room first-rate for the typist

parts.note: empty room is space

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word rate is taken

explanation.surface: A typist is offered an excellent empty room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-rate' looks like praise, but it means the first letter of 'rate'. The answer is the space bar of a typewriter.
explanation.definitionFit: On a typewriter the bar that leaves a gap between words is a tool used in typing.

clue.text: The main movement

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea, and its movement is its rise and fall

explanation.definitionFit: The sea's regular ebb and flow is caused by the moon.

clue.text: Subject on which the girl's not quite finished writing

indicators.note: the following piece is added after the first one

parts.note: it is a subject pronoun, a word that can be the subject of a sentence

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl has not completed her essay on a set topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite finished' cuts ALICE to ALIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type modelled on handwriting is a style of script or lettering.

clue.text: Mad plot I devised with man from the embassy

indicators.note: devised means worked out or contrived, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An envoy is caught hatching a crazy scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges MADPLOTI.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy serving abroad represents his country at its mission there.

clue.text: Note bees swarming around river birds

indicators.note: the first pieces go about the next one

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: bees swarming move in a confused mass, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone notices bees swarming beside a river where water birds live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swarming' mixes BEES into EBES. 'river birds' tempts as the definition, but the river supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: These diving water fowl are a family of lake and river birds.

clue.text: Phone out of order when copy is required

parts.note: a broken device is dead
a line is a telephone connection

explanation.surface: A journalist's telephone stops working just as the article is due.
explanation.walkthrough: In journalism copy is the text to be printed, and it must arrive by a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: A time limit for submission is when an editor expects the text.
